how.limits.title: What this does not model
how.limits.intro: The scenarios use river flow only. Anything below can close a road without showing up here, so a crossing that is not flagged is “not flagged in this scenario”, never an assurance.
how.limits.surge: **Storm surge and tide.** Observed coastal water levels are shown separately in the nowcast. They are not combined with the river-flow scenarios.
how.limits.pluvial: **Street and drainage (pluvial) flooding** from rain that never reaches a stream.
how.limits.deck: **Road deck height**, and **debris and scour** at a crossing.
how.limits.islands: **Service-island cutoffs.** Areas that lose their route without a modeled stream crossing closing, such as the Smithville Island area served by Dosher Memorial Hospital on Brunswick County Emergency Management’s service-islands map, may not appear in a river-flow-only replay.
how.limits.islandsnote: Brunswick County Emergency Management’s service-islands map is a modeled reference, not an observation of what happened.

about.title: About and limits
about.meta.description: What Lifelines does, how it was tested, and what it does not claim.
about.notice: Not for emergency use. In an emergency, call 911. This is a scenario and nowcast tool for a student pilot, not a warning service.
about.does.title: What it does
about.does.body: Most flood tools answer “is this road underwater?” Lifelines asks a different question: if a river crossing closes, can this neighborhood still reach an emergency room, fire station, dialysis center or other lifeline, and when does that change? It joins NOAA National Water Model streamflow, USGS and NWS gauges, NOAA tide stations, 2,920 road crossings and a road network of about 246,000 segments with 11 emergency hospitals, 220 fire stations and a topped-up list of dialysis, nursing-home, urgent-care, police, EMS and pharmacy sites in New Hanover, Brunswick and Pender counties, North Carolina. The address check shows what is observed now and then the forecast, and also a the Florence replay for testing.

about.testing.title: What testing showed
about.testing.intro: Tests were written down before the data was pulled, run once, and the failures are published too.
about.test1.text: AUC: river flow at the hours flooded-road reports were filed, versus ordinary hours (74 reports, 66 crossings). Shows storm versus not-storm, not which road.
about.test2.text: of 73 gauge-storms: modeled peak flow within a factor of 2 of USGS gauges, median peak-time error 4 hours.
about.test3.text: of 150 test blocks: baseline drive time to the nearest hospital within 30% of OSRM.
about.test4.text: AUC across nine 2023 to 2025 NC storm windows: crossings near recorded closures ranked higher. Precision is low (about 5%).
about.test5.text: AUC: the 11 Brunswick crossings on the Sheriff’s known-flood-point map rank above 1,435 other Brunswick crossings by people affected (11 crossings, one county).
about.case.title: Case study: Florence, Brunswick County
about.case.p1: The Brunswick County Sheriff’s Office marked 20 known flood points on its 2018 evacuation map. We matched 12 of the 20 to 11 road crossings and checked them against our road model.
about.case.p2: Take point 10, the NC 211 (Southport-Supply Rd) bridge over Lockwoods Folly River near Supply. Close it and 4,681 people in 128 Census blocks, all in the Sheriff’s Town Creek island, can no longer reach the nearest emergency room the way they do now, Novant Health Brunswick Medical Center. With all 11 matched crossings closed, those people go from an average of 12.6 minutes to the nearest ER to 24.3 minutes (+11.7); 3,242 of them are 10 minutes or more slower and 370 are 15 minutes or more slower. The worst block goes from 7.7 to 24.8 minutes, when the nearest ER becomes J. Arthur Dosher Memorial Hospital in Southport.
about.case.alt: Map of the Supply and Southport area in Brunswick County. The NC 211 bridge over Lockwoods Folly River is marked closed; dots for 128 Census blocks south and east of it are colored by added minutes to the nearest emergency room, mostly 8 to 17 minutes more, with Novant Health Brunswick Medical Center to the west and J. Arthur Dosher Memorial Hospital in Southport to the east.
about.case.caption: The 128 blocks this one bridge slows by more than a minute, colored by added minutes in the run with all 11 matched crossings closed (`block_deltas.csv`).
about.case.p3: The model picks out the crossings that matter. The 11 matched crossings rank above the other 1,435 assessed Brunswick crossings by people affected (AUC 0.77, 95% CI 0.61 to 0.90): the places the Sheriff’s Office flagged are the places where losing a crossing slows the most people.
about.case.p4: The flood-point map is dated 11 September 2018, before landfall, so the points are known flood spots. The islands map is dated 9 October 2018. Full report: [reports/phase2_bcso_islands.md](https://github.com/nishaanthjay/CAC-Lifelines-Lifelines/blob/main/reports/phase2_bcso_islands.md).
about.claim.title: What we do not claim
about.claim2: We do not claim forecast skill. Every validation test is a hindcast or an operational-analysis replay.
about.claim3: We never say a road, block or address is safe. A road that is not flagged is “not flagged in this scenario”, never an all-clear.
about.claim4: Scenarios use river flow only: no storm surge, tide, street flooding, bridge deck height, scour or debris.
about.claim8: Address results are estimates from the nearest Census block, not the exact address.
about.claim9: 1,333 of the 1,583 assessed crossings are OpenStreetMap road-stream intersections that may not be bridges; the route page lets you leave them out. Dialysis, nursing-home, urgent-care, police and pharmacy lists come from federal / HHS files (dated per entry) and OpenStreetMap, EMS stations from OpenStreetMap only: all incomplete, none confirmed open. There is no shelter list.
about.claim10: The live forecast is the NOAA National Water Model short-range run, unvalidated and river flow only. Observed gauge readings (nowcast) are shown beside it, not merged into route status.
about.privacy.title: Data and privacy
about.privacy.body: No account and no user data stored. Addresses you type go to OpenStreetMap Nominatim and routes to the public Valhalla router; neither is kept by us. Sources: NOAA, USGS, NCDOT, FEMA, US Census, CMS, NC OSFM, OpenStreetMap contributors, OpenFreeMap. Hourly NOAA forecast cycles are archived in an open repository: github.com/nishaanthjay/lifelines-nvm-archive.
